claims.text: Equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has low hardness and strength.
The early onset of deformation twinning is the main mechanism governing the low hardness and strength of CoCrFeNiTi.
Low stacking-fault energy promotes deformation twinning through dislocation dissociation.
Dissociated dislocations meeting on adjacent slip planes form deformation twins.
Twin boundaries and dissociated dislocations accommodate strain without significant work hardening.
Deformation twinning enhances ductility at the expense of hardness and strength.
The applicable composition is equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi can exist as a single-phase FCC alloy.
The proposed initial state contains no secondary precipitates.
Intensive cold rolling produces a nanostructured state with a high deformation-twin density.
Re-annealing restores a coarse-grained CoCrFeNiTi structure with minimal deformation-induced twinning.
Deformation twins act as localized strain accommodators rather than effective barriers to dislocation motion.
The strain-accommodation role of twins reduces work-hardening capacity.
Reduced work-hardening capacity causes lower hardness and ultimate tensile strength.
Cold-rolled nanostructured samples will have more deformation twins than re-annealed coarse-grained samples.
Cold-rolled nanostructured samples will have lower yield strength, hardness, and work-hardening rates than re-annealed coarse-grained samples.
The mechanism applies at room temperature and moderate strain rates while the alloy remains single-phase FCC.
The mechanism may cease to apply after secondary-phase formation, at significantly elevated temperatures, or at extreme strain rates.
Solid-solution strengthening from lattice distortion may also contribute and has not been quantitatively separated from twinning.

contradictions.description: The material_initial_state identifies the starting state as nanostructured and potentially cold-rolled, whereas the baseline identifies coarse-grained material with minimal twinning as the reference state. Thus, the hypothesis does not consistently define which microstructure is the starting state.
